summary: CLI certificate login fails with limited RBAC after Okta identity migration
description:
Issue summary:
CLI users who authenticate with client certificates are able to establish a session after last week's Okta identity migration, but their effective RBAC scopes are truncated (missing several delegated groups). Affected users see 403s when calling the runbook and deploy APIs even though their principal is authenticated.

Impact:
- Several infra engineers cannot run elevated runbooks or deploy to staging/production from CLI.
- Blocker for oncall rota: runbook elevation and emergency deploys.

Environment:
- Production, us-west region.
- CLI auth path uses client-cert -> sso-proxy -> identity-mapper -> rbac-service.

Observed symptoms:
- Successful client-cert TLS handshake and SSO assertion exchange.
- RBAC tokens returned with missing delegated group claims (group list truncated to first 2 entries).
- Console web login for same users functions normally.

Discovery timeline:
- 2026-03-10 08:45 reporter alerted #support about failed runbook run.
- 2026-03-10 09:10 SRE confirmed certificate authentication step succeeded but authorization failed.
- 2026-03-11 engineers correlated with Okta identity migration performed 2026-03-09 23:00 which introduced new session issuer TTL and claim encoding.
- 2026-03-12 quick workaround deployed (client-cert rebind script) restored access for a subset of users.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use pre-migration client cert/profile (or new cert) to run: rw-cli login --cert /path/to/cert.pem
3) Run a restricted command that requires delegated runbook access: rw-cli runbook execute --id emergency-db-rollback
5) Inspect /var/log/sso-proxy/auth.log for the auth flow and identity-mapper logs for claim set.
expected_behavior: Authenticated CLI sessions should receive the full set of delegated group claims and be authorized against runbook/deploy endpoints the same as console/web sessions.
actual_behavior: Client-cert authentication completes but the downstream identity-mapper returns a truncated groups array (only first two groups), causing RBAC to deny elevated operations.
logs: [2026-03-10T09:11:02Z] sso-proxy: tls: client certificate verified: subject=CN=eng-alice@example.com
[2026-03-10T09:11:02Z] sso-proxy: exchanged assertion with idp, assertion-issuer=okta, assertion-id=0a1b2c
[2026-03-10T09:11:03Z] identity-mapper: mapped principal alice@example.com, groups=[infra-oncall, infra-deploy] (expected 8 groups)
[2026-03-10T09:11:03Z] rbac-service: authorization denied for alice@example.com on runbook: missing required group infra-runbooks-admin -> 403 insufficient_scope
comments: Aisha Kapoor (reporter) - 2026-03-10: Noticed first customer-facing unblock case; affected user had valid cert and previously working CLI flow.

Diego Morales (assignee) - 2026-03-10: Initial triage - authentication succeeds, looks like an identity claim population issue between identity-mapper and rbac-service. Pulling logs and checking Okta migration notes.

SRE-Team (channel #sre) - 2026-03-11: Confirmed Okta migration changed assertion 'groups' encoding from JSON array to comma-delimited string for assertions issued by the new pool. Identity-mapper had no handling for the new shape in CLI flow.
Identity (PR author) - 2026-03-12: Raised PR to identity-mapper to normalize group claim to array and added defensive parsing. Deployed to staging for validation.

Diego Morales - 2026-03-12: Deployed a hotfix to identity-mapper in prod: parse both array and comma-delimited strings. Partial restoration observed. Follow-up: audit tokens older than migration window for stale encoded sessions.
Oncall-Eng (alice@example.com) - 2026-03-12: Verified workaround (rw-cli cert-rebind) rebinds a new session and regained runbook access. Logged steps in the ticket.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis: Okta migration changed claim serialization for group attributes in the assertion issuer pool used by CLI certificates (pool-id: okta-cli-pool-09).
Confirmed that web/OIDC flow uses a different assertion path that still returns group as an array, which explains why console users are unaffected.
Identity-mapper library v1.3.2 assumes groups claim is JSON array; v1.3.2 used by sso-proxy in CLI path did not attempt to coerce string -> array.
Telemetry: ~14 distinct engineers hit the failure between 2026-03-09 23:30 and 2026-03-11 02:00 UTC. Peak impact window aligns with migration cutover.
Risk: Some long-lived CLI sessions still have legacy assertion shape; token refresh path must be addressed to avoid recurrence.
Related config: Okta assertion mapping change documented in internal changelog: https://confluence.redwood.ai/ops/okta-migrations/2026-03-09
resolution: Workaround: instructed affected engineers to run 'rw-cli cert-rebind' which forces a fresh assertion exchange and results in normalized group claim. Hotfix: identity-mapper parsing change deployed to prod (2026-03-12) to accept both array and comma-delimited group claims. Full fix scheduled to add schema validation + unit tests in identity-mapper release v1.3.3.
follow_up_actions: 1) Add assertion shape validation to identity-mapper and reject/alert on unexpected shapes (owner: Identity Team, due 2026-03-18).
2) Backfill short-lived session refresh to normalize claims for active CLI sessions (owner: SRE, due 2026-03-17).
3) Add automated e2e test for CLI cert flow that validates group claim mapping across Okta pools (owner: QA, due 2026-03-20).
4) Postmortem draft linking to Okta migration notes and mitigation steps (owner: Diego Morales, due 2026-03-19).
